correctness.rationale: PASS: Polygonal secondary-polytope construction gives an equivariant polar associahedral sphere S(V_n) in R^n orthogonal to constants and two first Fourier harmonics (dimension n-3, sphere dimension n-4). The fixed dimension for C_q is n-3 if q=1 and m-1 otherwise, where m=n/q. For D_{q,a} the residual reflection j→a-j on m classes has f(m,a) solutions of 2j=a mod m, hence orbit count (m+f)/2; subtract invariants of constant plus first harmonic as appropriate to obtain claimed S^{(n+f)/2-3} or S^{(m+f)/2-2}. For n>=6 the sphere is simply connected; by Armstrong, π1 quotient is H modulo normal subgroup generated by fixed-point elements. Proper rotation subgroup generator fixes a point; full rotations r^b stabilize iff gcd(n,b)>=2; their exponents generate index 2 iff n is a 2-power, otherwise gcd(2,oddprime)=1; individual reflections always fix points and generate every dihedral subgroup. Thus stated π1/H1 holds. Independently enumerated 1,436 finite subgroup permutation-orbit fixed-dimension checks for even n through 50; the theorem is established by representation arithmetic and Armstrong, not this finite test.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: Reiner’s equivariant fiber-polytope theory supplies the natural sphere and invariant subpolytopes, and Armstrong supplies the generic quotient π1 formula; these are credited. The exact complete all-even-n every-subgroup fixed-space dimensions and sharp n=2^e exception are not literally stated or implied without the new stabilizer arithmetic in inspected sources. Published odd-prime associahedral lens quotients and prime-power bidirected polygon multipaths concern disjoint parameter or distinct complex.
